newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Henderson sees HK home prices stablising.
newsitem.headline: Henderson sees HK home prices stablising.

text.p: Henderson Land Development Co Ltd chairman Lee Shau-kee said on Wednesday residential property prices in Hong Kong should stablise after falling five to 10 percent in the secondary market since early March.
"Property prices in the secondary market have fallen five to 10 percent in April from (their levels) in early March," Lee told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"The prices should stabilise after the recent adjustment," he said.
Developers take secondary market prices as a guide when setting prices for new flat sales.
Lee also said Henderson Land would not be bidding as aggressively as last year in government land auctions this year due to the current high level of prices.
"We had been quite aggressive in land auctions before, but we eased off recently due to high prices," Lee said.
Henderson Land bought a number of government sites in last year's auctions, accounting for about 20 to 30 percent of the total amount sold, the chairman added.
"Even if we do not buy any more land, we still have a sufficient land bank for use in the next five years," Lee said.
The company had a good reserve of agricultural land which could be developed into residential units with a total floor area of between two and three million square feet, he said.
